NEWS FROM THE BOARD December 2024 NEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Tom Dayley - Commissioner Rod Beck - Board Chairman Ryan Davidson - Commissioner ADA COUNTY OFFICIALS BREAK GROUND ON THE PARK AT EXPO IDAHO Great things are happening in Ada County that will benefit families and individuals for generations. Ada County Commissioners, along with key county staff and distinguished guests, broke ground on Phase I of The Park at Expo Idaho on December 18, 2024. The 50-plus-acre park transforms the old racehorse track into a destination riverside park that prioritizes urban biodiversity, year-round active recreation, and nature-based play. Phase 2 of the project, The Fields at Expo Idaho, will include an additional 38 acres of sports fields and active recreation facilities.

# Page 2^page=2
The Park at Expo Idaho restores the site’s connection to the Boise River floodplain. Hydraulic and topographic interventions reintroduce historic watercourses, creating wetland habitats, improving water quality, and boosting biodiversity. All of this is happening on Ada County’s 240-acre Expo Idaho property which has been a treasured part of the community for decades. The Expo Idaho property is home to the annual Western Idaho Fair and draws more than a million visitors each year for trade shows, sporting events, public gatherings, concerts, agricultural events, and more. The best thing about all the improvements taking place – the Western Idaho Fair will stay right where it is! The Park at Expo Idaho demonstrates how thoughtful, yet ambitious design can transform disused urban spaces into civic destinations that enhance natural systems and elevate community vitality. When The Park at Expo Idaho is complete in 2026, this once-in-a-generation destination park will include: The Lowlands – a 17-acre restored floodplain with more than 1.4 miles of stream channels. ● The Ridges – topographic landforms framing the park’s perimeter created from the soil excavated from the Lowlands. ● Nature Playground – a multi-sensory play environment inspired by the Boise River’s riparian landscapes. ● All Wheel Sports Garden – an active wheel sports venue for users of all skill levels woven into a woodland landscape. ● 2

DONNA LEE 25 YEARS OF SERVICE Donna’s first day was on December 15th, 1999, in the Traffic Court on Barrister, next to the Sheriff’s office. She started at the filings window and soon after, she worked the “circular desk”. At that time, it was the hub where all video arraignments and notices were set up once defendants got out of court. From there she went to work the priority & non- priority papers desk and judgments. She also processed Warrants and with the jail next door, she would personally hand deliver them to the Sheriff’s Office. After moving to the downtown courthouse, she has since worked criminal records, summonses, the workloads desk (this was when we had paper files to get up to the judges for court for the week) entering citations, exonerating bonds and spending almost 15+ years on defaults & suspensions. Donna has so much knowledge within the criminal realm of the Clerk’s Office. As you can see, she has pretty much done it all and seen it all! She has been through all the court management systems, from AS400, to ISTARS, to Odyssey; and then Navigator, and lastly, Enterprise Justice. Donna is an outstanding employee and has been such a steady asset to the Clerk’s Office for the last 25 years! Congratulations on this incredible milestone! 6 JANINE KORSEN 30 YEARS OF SERVICE Janine launched her lengthy career with Ada County on December 5th, 1994. She began her journey in the old Ada County courthouse as a civil clerk for the Magistrate division. A short 9 months later, Janine was promoted to an In-Court Clerk for the newly appointed District Court Judge, Daniel T. Eismann. Janine worked with Judge Eismann for 5 years until his appointment as a Supreme Court Justice in May of 2000. Judge Eismann’s District Court position was filled by the Honorable Darla Williamson for whom Janine clerked for approximately 11 ½ years. Upon Judge Williamson’s retirement in 2011, Janine continued her career with Ada County clerking for Judge Lynn Norton, where she remains today. Janine also worked the Ada County elections for 20 of her 30 years. Janine has thrived under the leadership of 4 separate Clerks of the Court: Dave Navarro, Chris Rich, Phil McGrane, and now Trent Tripple. She is a pioneer, forging through great change throughout the years to include, but not limited to, learning 3 separate case management systems: AS400, ISTARS, and now Odyssey. She has progressed from typing cases into old docket books to the fully digitized system we use today. Janine recalls having to type court minutes into a word document and recording sessions on cassette tapes. Janine’s dedication to her Judges and the court system reflects in everything she does. She willingly shares her vast knowledge of court processes and procedures with less seasoned clerks, and consistently displays a delightful disposition in doing so. It has been our great privilege to have Janine on our Ada County District Court team. Thank you, Janine, for your dedication and service to Ada County. ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes thirteen individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks & waterways, indigent services, juvenile services, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County www.adacounty.id.gov/ 6
